questions.subject: Pre-vocational Studies
questions.topic: Safety Measures in Handling Agricultural Tools/Equipment
questions.learningObjective: Identify suitable reporting and instruction-checking decisions in fictional agricultural tool situations.
questions.prompt: Before a garden lesson, Efe notices that a tool handle is loose. Another pupil offers to hold it together while Efe works. State a safe decision and explain why the offer should be refused.

questions.explanation: Damage should be reported rather than improvised around by pupils.

questions.topic: Safety in Handling Home Economics Tools and Equipment
questions.learningObjective: Explain safety as reducing the chance of harm when handling Home Economics tools and equipment.
questions.prompt: In a Home Economics lesson, what does safety in handling tools mean? Explain it using a precaution taken before a task rather than a response after someone is hurt.
questions.answer: Safety means reducing the chance of harm. For example, checking for visible damage and asking the teacher about a fault before use can prevent an accident.
questions.explanation: Safety includes preventing harm, not merely treating its consequences.

markingGuide.description: Explains reduction/prevention of harm. Accept equivalent accurate wording.

questions.subject: Pre-vocational Studies
questions.topic: Safety in Handling Home Economics Tools and Equipment
questions.learningObjective: Explain safety as reducing the chance of harm when handling Home Economics tools and equipment.
questions.prompt: A group says, “Nobody was hurt yesterday, so our tool routine must be safe.” Explain why that conclusion is unreliable and what should be checked instead.
questions.answer: One injury-free occasion does not show that hazards are controlled. Check whether equipment is suitable and undamaged, instructions and precautions are followed, and the work area is safe.
questions.explanation: A near miss or chance outcome is not proof of a sound routine.

markingGuide.description: Rejects the inference from one injury-free occasion. Accept equivalent accurate wording.

questions.subject: Pre-vocational Studies
questions.topic: Safety in Handling Home Economics Tools and Equipment
questions.learningObjective: Outline selected safe decisions about damaged tools, unsuitable equipment and obstructions; no practical handling.
questions.prompt: A laundry demonstration is planned beside a doorway blocked by bags. Before any equipment is brought out, what change should be made to the area and which risk does it reduce?
questions.answer: Have the bags put in a suitable place so the doorway and route are clear. This reduces trips and obstruction of movement.
questions.explanation: Preparing the area is a precaution before equipment use.

markingGuide.description: Clears the doorway/route by suitable bag storage. Accept equivalent accurate wording.

questions.subject: Pre-vocational Studies
questions.topic: Safety in Handling Home Economics Tools and Equipment
questions.learningObjective: Outline selected safe decisions about damaged tools, unsuitable equipment and obstructions; no practical handling.
questions.prompt: A pupil says wearing gloves makes any kitchen or sewing tool suitable for a child to try. Explain why this is wrong and name who should decide whether a planned classroom activity is suitable.
questions.answer: Gloves do not remove all hazards or establish suitability. The teacher/responsible adult must check the actual tool, instructions, pupil needs and safe arrangements; unsuitable activities must not go ahead.
questions.explanation: Protective equipment cannot turn every activity into an appropriate pupil task.

markingGuide.description: Explains that gloves leave other hazards/suitability questions. Accept equivalent accurate wording.

questions.subject: Pre-vocational Studies
questions.topic: Safety in Handling Home Economics Tools and Equipment
questions.learningObjective: Explain inspection, reporting and suitable care instructions without repairing or maintaining actual equipment.
questions.prompt: A classroom equipment plan says, “Check each item before the lesson; put everything straight back after the lesson.” Explain why checking before use does not replace care after use. Add one missing after-use step to the written plan.
questions.answer: Use can leave an item dirty, wet or newly damaged even if it was sound beforehand. Before storage, arrange appropriate cleaning/drying or report any new damage, following the actual item’s instructions and the teacher’s arrangements.
questions.explanation: Inspection before use and suitable care after use occur at different stages; neither is a substitute for the other. This is a paper plan, not pupil cleaning or repair.

markingGuide.description: Explains a change that can occur during use, such as dirt, moisture or new damage. Accept equivalent accurate wording.
Adds an appropriate after-use care or fault-reporting step, with no universal washing or pupil repair instruction. Accept equivalent accurate wording.

questions.subject: Pre-vocational Studies
questions.topic: Safety in Handling Home Economics Tools and Equipment
questions.learningObjective: Explain inspection, reporting and suitable care instructions without repairing or maintaining actual equipment.
questions.prompt: A general classroom note says “wash tools before storage.” May a pupil apply it to every Home Economics item, including an electrical iron? Explain what must guide the care decision instead.
questions.answer: No. A general note is not a care method for every material or electrical appliance. The responsible adult must use the correct item’s instructions and suitable safety arrangements; pupils should not try washing an iron.
questions.explanation: Tool-specific instructions limit broad maintenance slogans.

markingGuide.description: Rejects applying one wash rule to every item/electrical iron. Accept equivalent accurate wording.
Requires actual-item instructions and responsible adult control. Accept equivalent accurate wording.
